title: Gold Gains After Fed’s Waller Reiterates Call for July Rate Cut
content: Gold gained after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller hinted that he would dissent if his colleagues vote to hold interest rates steady at their July meeting, making his case for a rate cut to support the labor market.

title: Reliance Profit Jumps 78%, Beats Estimate on One-Time Gain
content: Reliance Industries Ltd.’s quarterly profit beat estimates as the billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate benefited from a massive one-time gain from divesting its stake in India’s biggest paints maker.

title: Bond Yields Drop on Waller’s Call, Inflation Views: Markets Wrap
content: Bond yields fell alongside the dollar as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller reiterated his case for a July rate cut, while data showed an improvement in consumer expectations for inflation. Stocks fluctuated as traders parsed a handful of earnings.

title: Treasuries Extend Advance After Fed’s Waller Backs July Rate Cut
content: Treasury yields edged lower Friday after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller reiterated his case for an interest-rate cut this month, though traders still put the odds of one near zero.

title: Chevron Closes Hess Deal After Winning Exxon Fight
content: Chevron Corp. closed its $53 billion deal to buy Hess Corp. more than 20 months after the takeover was announced, after winning its arbitration battle with Exxon Mobil Corp. Chevron CEO Mike Wirth discusses the deal and says the resolution is good for the oil industry.

title: US Stocks Fluctuate as Netflix’s Slide Offsets Gains Elsewhere

title: Egypt Plans $4 Billion in International Bonds Over Next Year
content: Egypt plans to issue $4 billion of international bonds over the next 12 months, seeking to diversify its financing sources while overhauling the economy after the worst crisis in a generation.

title: Prices Drop on $2.7 Billion of Bonds Tied to Warehouse Leases

title: US Consumer Sentiment Rises to a Five-Month High
content: US consumer sentiment rose to a five-month high in early July as expectations about the economy and inflation continued to improve. The preliminary July sentiment index rose to 61.8 from 60.7 a month earlier, according to University of Michigan data. Mike McKee reports on “Bloomberg Open Interest.”
